read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of reader/data/route-store of the main branch at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4 (its index.json), for "Semantic Dictionary of Biblical Hebrew via HiperBiblia" (M17): 14,823 routes (axis: routes), 3,659 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row is the source's summary of the entry (its field summary), read only to understand a route: it equals the route text on 872 routes, and every route is one item of it, the items parted by its semicolons (axis: routes); the store's cut flag stands on 547 of them. The source audit compares each route with the lane's copy of the source, the file hiperbiblia-sdbh.json in ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/hiperbiblia-sdbh-2026-07-12/ (taken from hiperbiblia.com on 12 July 2026 AD, 8,934 records, "UBS Dictionary of Biblical Hebrew adapted from SDBH") through the store's 5,830 records of it: all 14,823 routes are an item of a summary on their own key and stand in the part of the entry's text that lists its senses, 10,095 of them as a whole rendering beside a middle dot, which parts the renderings of one sense there (axis: routes). Not every item has a route: of the 15,055 items those records hold in their summaries (axis: items, each counted once under its letters key), 14,823 stand as a route on their key and 232 do not: 36 on keys that hold other routes, and 196 under the 164 letters keys of the 168 entries whose headword holds a space or a maqaf, keys that hold no route at all (26 of those texts stand as a route under another letters key). So each route is one item of the source's list for its word, and for the routes that exist this dictionary is the ask's case of a store that already gives each sense its own route; the audit is evidence about the source and no part of any test. The source's own key to its signs: none found. The copy holds the fields id, headword, summary, part_of_speech, full_entry_text, source_url, license, source_year for each entry and at its head only run_date, index_url, definition_basis, license, index_pages_scanned, index_entry_ids, entry_pages_fetched, fetch_errors, with no front matter and no account of a sign. The README of the work it adapts (ubsicap/ubs-open-license at commit 3a6edd82, dictionaries/hebrew; in the lane's cache at ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/ubs-sdbh-hebrew-2026-07-15/) explains its encoded tags and lists abbreviations of cited works, and gives no account of any mark a route of this dictionary holds. So every shape of this ledger begins "unverified:", but for those of the apostrophe and the hyphen, which are plain English spelling.

definitions.terms: In every test a character is one Unicode code point; every route of this dictionary holds only characters from U+0020 to U+007E, so a code point and a JavaScript string index are the same thing here. A letter is one of a to z or A to Z. A space is the character U+0020 only, and no test uses whitespace of any other kind. Nothing is trimmed: the text is the whole route text as it stands, which is the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def; the text before and the text after the mark are the parts of it on either side of the mark, without the mark. The character directly before or after the mark is none at the start or the end of the text, and none is not a letter. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it; a stop or comma outside them belongs to the sentence. Exactly means character for character, and every string and list minds case. Begins with, ends in and contains look at characters only and need no word end; contains finds a run of characters anywhere. The container is the template's c.container and a test looks at it only where its words say so.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence, and no later shape is tried for it. Not caught above means that no earlier shape of the same mark took the occurrence. A shape's container field is not part of its test: the checker compares it afterwards.
definitions.pair_sides: For a round bracket that has a partner: what the pair holds is the text between the opening and the closing bracket (the template's c.group). The pair's left side is the text before its opening bracket. The pair's right side is the text after its closing bracket. The opening and the closing bracket of a pair are tried against the same tests, in the same order, and no route holds a round bracket inside a round bracket.
definitions.marked_cuts_rule: Each entry of side_by_side_cuts is one route's text, exact to the character, with the three characters space, pipe, space written directly before each mark the branch may cut. An occurrence stands at a mark of the list when the whole text is exactly an entry once all that entry's ' | ' are taken out, and in that entry a ' | ' stands directly before this occurrence: the occurrence's index in the text equals the index of that ' | ' in the entry less three for each ' | ' before it. A route's other marks, the sign that closes the last part of a series among them, are not at a mark of the list.

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number. The source's own file gives every entry an id, which the store keeps only on its record and the route store dropped; two entries under one letters key stand there as separate texts with nothing to tell them apart (example key אדר: its route texts come from the source's entries H142 and H145). keys_with_more_than_one_route_text counts renderings of one sense, senses and homonyms together. By the audit, of the 3,004 such keys (axis: keys; 3,659 letters keys in all), 1,834 are keys under which the store's records hold one entry of the source and 1,170 keys under which they hold more than one.

branches.question: Inside one row the source sometimes writes two or more words side by side, each of which could render the Hebrew alone, like: joy, delight. Should each be its own reading? Each row is one item of the source's own list for its word, so words side by side in one row may mean nearly the same thing, and no test can tell when they do not; these rows stand in a written list. The same question covers words parted by a question mark, an exclamation mark or a colon (horn? trumpet?). Rows whose words lean on each other (to be, become weak; mouth of well, cave, pit) are not in the list and stay as one reading under either answer.

options.means: The page prints each part as its own reading, without the sign between them: joy, and delight. A bracket stays with the part it touches, even where it may speak of every part: serious, and grievous (suffering). A question mark or an exclamation mark at a cut is not printed, so only the last part keeps its sign: horn? trumpet? prints horn, and trumpet?
The page prints the row as one reading, as the source writes it: joy, delight.

branches.question: The source sometimes writes a wording, an equals sign, and what the wording means, like: "straight way" = safe journey. Should the wording and what it means be two readings? The source writes the same thing with the sign > too (blood > bloodshed), but that sign counts as a bracket with no partner, and a text with such a bracket is never cut, so those rows print as one reading under either answer. An equals sign inside a bracket (to catch up with (= happen)) or at the very start of a row also stays as it is under either answer.

options.means: The page prints the wording as one reading and what it means as another, without the equals sign: "straight way", and safe journey. Any quotation marks stay on the wording.
The page prints the wording and what it means as one reading, as the source writes them.

not_done_here: This ledger leaves to the store the semicolons of the source's summary, at each of which the store has already made a new route, so that no route holds one (2 routes come from a cut inside a round bracket) and every route that holds no mark, because a shape stands only at a mark, so the rows that read NO DATA YET (2 routes; axis: routes) stand as they are; it leaves to the ask's rule 3 the 193 routes that hold the sign > (axis: routes), which stay whole; it leaves to the page the step that the answer no_pill of B03 asks for, since a declaration can cut a row and has no field that leaves a whole row out; and it strikes nothing, naming in store-questions-v1.jsonl the rows and items it asks the store about.
